Though I enjoyed 6 1/2 enough to upvote it, I'm much in-line with other critters here in that I quickly lost interest. I felt hopelessly lost in the beginning of the tale, as I'd just watched this character recover from physical trauma, yet they were now experiencing memetic issues. I feel this should have been more clearly acknowledged in the previous tale.

Beyond that, it felt aimless and somewhat repetitive. I'd gone into this thinking something was going to happen from the events of the previous tale, but it ends up being more backstory that doesn't feel like it develops the character or push the narrative onward in any significant way.

I don't read tales often so my expectations might be a bit different to more seasoned readers, but I really dig this! I like Shiloh and their struggles, and both parts show the pretty grim implications of working for the Foundation - I especially love the cognitohazard training.

+1

item.content:encoded:
I unfortunately have to agree with the negative critiques. The tale just doesn't flow very well to me, and I think it could benefit from some severe cutdowns in order to remove bloat. While the start is interesting enough, more than half of the story is dedicated to Shiloh's recovery. Their story is, on the surface, compelling enough, but the way that the story is told drags for me. The way that it's presented seems more of a recap summary of events as opposed to a narrative flow; we are told too much of what is happening, which doesn't interest me nearly as much as Shiloh as a character, who is fairly interesting on their own.

I don't think that a story necessarily needs a grand cacophony of fireworks and prose per se, but character driven pieces need a healthy dose of characterization, and this story focuses far too much on re-telling events rather than on the characters. I think this piece would work a lot better if it were significantly reduced in bloat and really honed in on a character-driven piece that isn't quite as long. As such, the summary of events loses the audience's interest and doesn't make me excited to keep going.

item.content:encoded:
I honestly didn't enjoy this at all. Your first tale was okay, but this one feels completely disconnected from it and is kind of a pain to read through. I lost interest very quickly, to the point where I didn't care about the characters or feel like the article would be a rewarding experience at all.

EDIT: To clarify, I don't have an issue with this standing on its own, and I encourage tales that are part of a series to be able to remain independent in some way. My issue is that by being part of a series, it's subject to certain expectations. This fails to expound upon the previous tale at all, and doesn't answer any questions. It simply feels like a completely separate story which happens to have some of the same characters.
